artworks.title: Thamyris and the Muses (hydria)
artworks.description: Attic hydria: Thamyris among the Muses before the contest that costs him sight and song — the Thracian bard as vase-painting cautionary tale.

artworks.title: Thamyris (vase detail)
artworks.description: A closer view of the same hydria type: the musician who challenged the Muses — lyre still in hand at the edge of hubris.

artworks.title: Thamyris and the Muses
artworks.description: Another Attic vase of Thamyris with the Muses — the challenge scene repeated for another symposium, the bard forever about to lose his voice.

popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Book II — Homer recalls Thamyris of Thrace, blinded by the Muses after boasting he could outsing them.

popCulture.title: Thamyris
popCulture.description: The Thracian minstrel who challenged the Muses and lost his sight and art — Greek myth's warning against artistic hubris.
